claim: In the uniform random-codebook additive-noise model with fixed rate 0<R<1 and codebook size 2^{floor(nR)}, consider subexponential lists with at least two entries and limiting first, second and last rank exponents y_1, y_2, y_L, where y_L<1. Assume finite point-likelihood decay rates g(y_1) and g(y_2) along the actual first and second rank sequences, with g(y)=I(y)+y, and assume the strict noise-rank tail beyond the actual last list rank has decay rate inf_{x>=y_L} I(x). Then Delta=min{g(y_2),1-R+inf_{x>=y_L} I(x)}-g(y_1) gives the off-critical posterior exponents: for Delta>0 the error probability decays at rate Delta, and for Delta<0 the success probability decays at rate -Delta.

integrity.computational_claims: No numerical computation or finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact random-codebook posterior formula and exponential-rate comparison.

scientific_limitations: Requires finite point-rank limits and the moving strict-tail limit explicitly stated in the finding. In the cited fixed-list framework, the estimates are supplied below the guesswork support endpoint H_0. A last-rank exponent below one does not by itself give a strict-tail estimate at H_0<1.
Applies to a uniform random-codebook additive-noise model with subexponential list size and last-rank exponent below one.
No conclusion at Delta=0 or for exponentially growing lists; arbitrary fixed codebooks are not covered.
title: Subexponential-list stability of rank-conditioned decoding reliability
